newsitem.title: USA: Zeigler Coal exploring financing on plant.
newsitem.headline: Zeigler Coal exploring financing on plant.

text.p: Zeigler Coal Holding Co said it continues to explore financing arrangements in order to proceed with plans to build a Liquids from Coal (LFC) plant in Wyoming.

The company also is engaged in discussions with potential equity partners. In the 1996 fourth quarter, Zeigler signed a construction contract for a full-scale LFC plant that would process about six million tons of coal feedstock a year.

Zeigler also said its transition toward lower sulfur coal continues. In the fourth quarter, one of its subsidiaries completed the acquisition of the Betsy Layne reserve in eastern Kentucky. The 17.5-million ton reserve is expected to begin production in the first half of 1997 and produce about one million tons of low-sulfur coal annually.

The company said its new energy trading and marketing subsidiary, EnerZ Corp, received approval in the fourth quarter from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission as a wholesale power marketer. EnerZ continues to add staff and talk with potential customers.

President Chand Vyas said the company's various projects "enabled us to make significant progress toward my stated '20-20 Vision' of growing revenues and total return to shareholders an average of 20 percent per year."
Earlier, Zeigler reported a fourth-quarter profit of $0.69 a share, which included a $0.03 a share charge from revaluation of stock appreciation units.
